comparator.name: Middle Eastern Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The live 2026–27 Leiden product confirms five active 180-EC routes: Arabic, Hebrew, Modern Middle East, Persian and Turkish language/culture. Modern Middle East Studies is selected before UCR review because it studies the region as a whole and is the broadest representation of the generic registry target. Its formal structure is 60 EC in each year. Year 1 combines a 30-EC common regional/humanities core with one complete 30-EC language option; Arabic is selected as the first-listed option. Year 2 contains 55 EC compulsory regional history, religion, anthropology, politics and political economy plus the first-listed 5-EC restricted choice. Year 3 contains 15 EC comparative literature/thesis preparation, a 5-EC route-specific slot, a 10-EC thesis and 30 EC open elective space. The current live product lists History of Central Asia & Afghanistan in both the Year 2 compulsory group and the Year 3 route-specific slot. Both official slots are disclosed separately to preserve the published 60/60/60 structure while explicitly flagging the apparent duplication; the reconstruction does not silently invent a replacement. The component total is 180 EC.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is generic Middle Eastern Studies. Of the five current official routes, Modern Middle East Studies has the broadest region-wide historical, cultural, religious, political and economic identity rather than centring one language/culture. It is selected on that academic basis before UCR availability is considered. Arabic is then selected from the route’s four first-year language packages by official listing order.

programmes.label: Middle Eastern Studies at Leiden University

exception.reason: A valid 24-course UCR programme cannot represent this bachelor’s defining combination of sustained Middle East-specific history, cultures, religions, politics and political economy with a mandatory 30-EC Arabic, Persian, Turkish or Hebrew language package. UCR has no Arabic, Persian, Turkish or Hebrew course or sequence, and its current catalogue contains no sustained Middle Eastern Studies curriculum. Filling 24 places with general history, international relations, law, sociology, literature or art would change the target into generic global studies and falsely imply regional and language preparation that UCR does not provide.
exception.curriculumContext: The selected current Modern Middle East Studies route totals 180 EC: 30 EC common first-year Middle East/humanities study, a complete 30-EC Arabic option, 55 EC compulsory second-year regional study, one 5-EC restricted choice, 20 EC third-year comparative literature/thesis preparation and route-specific study, a 10-EC bachelor thesis and 30 EC open elective space. The alternative first-year language packages are Persian, Turkish and Hebrew and create the same decisive language-depth mismatch. The live guide’s repeated placement of History of Central Asia & Afghanistan is disclosed in the comparator components rather than silently repaired.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026-cohort availability. The catalogue contains Dutch but no Arabic, Persian, Turkish or Hebrew. GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations mentions the Middle East only as one possible contemporary theatre within a general international-relations course. GOSHIST211 History of Empires, GOSPOLI313 Peace & Conflict, GOSLAWJ111 Human Rights: Law & Philosophy, GOSLAWJ212 Introduction to Public International Law and GOSSOCI214 Modern Sociology provide comparative frameworks, not a sustained regional curriculum. MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature touches Arabic literary traditions and MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean includes Islamic courts within broader cross-cultural study, but neither supplies Middle Eastern Studies breadth or language training. These isolated adjacent elements cannot support a defensible 24-course match to the programme’s region-specific and language-based identity.
